_note: CONFIG-02 permission data (D-03). Pure data — NO enforcement logic here. Consumed by tools/harness_perms/resolver.py (resolve_bash + resolve_path) and, in Phase 4, by the contract-guard / secret hooks that import that resolver verbatim. The 15 opencode permission keys each map to allow|ask|deny; `bash` is an INSERTION-ORDERED object encoding last-wins glob semantics (catch-all `*` FIRST, increasingly specific overrides after — never end with a broad `allow`, Pitfall P3). `path_deny_globs` are the constitution/secret path-scoped denies the resolver enforces (opencode's native `edit` key is not path-globbable, so path denies live here as data). The constitution subset is the FOUR members declared by docs/adr/0001-walking-skeleton-golden-core.md:48 — contracts/**, docs/adr/**, golden/** and the literal file docs/glossary.md; this data implements that accepted decision rather than defining it, so a member may not be added or dropped without a superseding ADR. docs/glossary.md is deliberately a literal path, not a docs/** tree: the plane is the glossary, not the docs directory, and it remains a HUMAN_CORPUS review target because constitution ownership (who may edit) and a review obligation (when a human owes a review) are orthogonal.
